additionalConflict.question: Establish which grant applies to the installed archive; do not automatically substitute the current repository license.

recoveryAttempts.method: Verified tarball -> declared repository -> immutable commit -> byte-for-byte match of a shipped file at that commit -> licence text at that same commit. The byte match is what makes the repository evidence for the artifact; without it the record would only assert that a licence exists in a repository sharing a name with the package.
recoveryAttempts.provenOnKnownGood: The builder reproduces both existing hand-made records exactly — boolbase@1.0.0 and tr46@0.0.3 — including integrity, commit, licence text and the overlapping runtime proof. That is the only evidence that its success path works at all, since none of the six below reached it.
recoveryAttempts.outcome: None of the six could be recovered mechanically, and each for a DIFFERENT reason. These are now specific human questions rather than an unexplained gap.

packages.detail: The package ships a BUILT dist/index.js. No shipped file matches the repository at that commit, so the repository cannot stand as evidence for these bytes. GitHub reports no licence file on the repository at all.
packages.question: Accept the manifest BSD-2-Clause declaration as the grant for a built artifact, or ask the author for a licence file?

packages.detail: This is the ONE package where the byte binding exists: the published eastasianwidth.js matches that commit exactly (sha256 2672ae17e3d91c24...). The repository has no tags, so the commit was found by comparing candidates against the published bytes. But there is no licence file at that commit — MIT-LICENSE.txt was added in 1d41951a59d63fb2d77cda021050fc070cae424a on 2024-06-05, roughly six and a half years after the release we install.
packages.question: Is the later MIT-LICENSE.txt admissible as the author stating the terms of an earlier release, or does the manifest declaration have to stand alone? A record was NOT written, because pairing 2024 text with 2017 bytes is exactly the kind of claim this evidence store exists to prevent.

packages.detail: Ships a built dist/highlightjs-vue.cjs.js which matches nothing at that commit. It also reproduces the conflict already recorded in additionalConflict from the other direction: the manifest declares CC0-1.0 and the repository is BSD-3-Clause. The tool now refuses this class outright — recording BSD text under a CC0 identifier would assert a grant nobody made.
packages.question: Unchanged from additionalConflict: establish which grant applies to the installed archive. Do not substitute the current repository licence.

packages.question: Ask the author which commit 2.3.8 was cut from, or accept the MIT declaration plus the repository LICENSE without a byte binding and say so explicitly in the record.
